At 4B, \cls{} and \cwm{} are separated by 1.18\pp{} on the matched three-seed subset. At 8B, the gap widens to 2.43\pp{} (Figure~\ref{fig:scaling_gap}). Clustered bootstrap yields a mean gap of 2.26\pp{} ($p = 0.0066$, 95\% CI $[1.80, 2.71]$), confirming the widening is not a sampling artifact.

The two formulations scale differently: from 4B to 8B, \cls{} gains +0.99\pp{} (88.41 $\to$ 89.40) while \cwm{} shows no statistically significant improvement ($-$0.27\pp{}, 87.23 $\to$ 86.96) under our experimental configuration (LoRA rank 16, fixed hyperparameters, 3 seeds). The \cwm{} regression falls within seed noise (3-seed std ${\sim}$0.5\pp{}) and could reflect suboptimal hyperparameter transfer at 8B rather than a fundamental scaling limitation. We do not claim that generation \emph{cannot} benefit from scale, only that it did not in this configuration. This pattern is observed within Qwen3 only; whether it generalizes across model families at function level is not yet tested. At repository-level complexity, the interaction between formulation and scale is examined in \S\ref{sec:repo}.

185	Two patterns account for the majority of unparseable \cwm{} outputs on Qwen3.
